output.summary: Perennial mint-family herb of unstated native origin, lesser calamint commonly grows around the Mediterranean, North Africa and parts of Central Asia. Its fragrant, grey-green leaves resemble oregano and smell of pennyroyal, while its flowers are lavender-pink. It is used as a culinary herb in Italian and Corsican cooking, including Roman-style artichokes and a southern Italian goat cheese.
